### Excessive memory allocation when decompressing crafted streams in github.com/andybalholm/brotli
BIT-brotli-2026-111497 / BIT-dotnet-2026-111497 / BIT-dotnet-sdk-2026-111497 / BIT-node-2026-111497 / BIT-node-min-2026-111497 / BIT-powershell-2026-111497 / [CVE-2026-111497](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-111497) / [GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35) / [GHSA-c9gr-gmg4-2vqv](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-c9gr-gmg4-2vqv) / [GO-2026-6888](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6888) / PYSEC-2026-4322 / PYSEC-2026-4323

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
In github.com/andybalholm/brotli before v1.2.7, the decompressor allocates memory for Huffman tables and block-type trees on every meta-block header without bounding the cumulative allocations relative to the input size. A small crafted brotli stream containing many empty meta-blocks with new Huffman trees can trigger hundreds of megabytes of allocations per kilobyte of input, leading to denial of service.

#### Severity
Unknown

#### References
- [https://github.com/andybalholm/brotli/security/advisories/GHSA-c9gr-gmg4-2vqv](https://redirect.github.com/andybalholm/brotli/security/advisories/GHSA-c9gr-gmg4-2vqv)
